title: Choose the visual world for PrepAhead
question: The roll assigned Tingkat Enamel. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Tingkat Enamel
options.lineage: Singapore enamel tiffin carriers and tingkat meal delivery
options.thesis: Lunch planned ahead, the way tingkat meals were: stacked tiers, counted before anyone cooks.
options.viewport: Both view: phone on the left, counter tablet on the right; the stall's header is filled with its enamel colour and the prep number sits beside a stack of tiers, history trays in white enamel, today's pre-orders filled in the stall colour.
options.risk: Tingkat is less familiar to Gen Z students than hawker signboards; it lands only if the tier stack is the clearest thing on screen.

raised.raise: State lives in form as well as colour: filled, outlined and dashed tiers read correctly in greyscale.
Enamel red is reserved for what needs a decision now: a new order, an uncollected pickup, cook another tray.
Every count sits against its limit in tabular numerals: 16 / 40 portions, 9 trays, 14 spare.
One number owns each panel at poster size (trays, code, minutes to cut-off), readable from over a shoulder.
Each stall owns one enamel colour everywhere it appears, so an order can be followed from phone to tablet by colour.

options.label: Hawker Signboard
options.lineage: lightbox signboards above canteen and hawker stalls
options.thesis: Every stall and every order reads like the lit signboard above the counter.
options.viewport: Stall list as a row of signboards with numbered plates and bilingual names; the dashboard header is the stall's own signboard with the prep number on its yellow price strip.
options.risk: Familiar: most local food concepts land here, and red with yellow can read as fast food.

options.label: Metro Tiles
options.thesis: Chrome deleted: stalls become flat colour tiles and the prep number goes poster size.
options.viewport: Black ground, stall tiles in four flat colours on the phone, a giant lowercase '9 trays' on the tablet with counts as tiles.
options.case: Holds product clarity: poster-size type reads across a table. Loses identification: nothing in it says NTU canteen.
options.risk: Reads as 2012 Windows Phone, and edge-cropped headlines fight the side-by-side view.

options.label: Emission-Line Rail
options.thesis: Every element hangs off one rail; state is line height and dash, not hue.
options.viewport: Orders as hairline ticks on one off-centre rail over charcoal.
options.case: Loses both: nobody at a canteen identifies with spectrograms, and one tiny type size fails over a shoulder.
options.kept: State carried by form, not colour alone.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: A fixed terrain of demand with the day's orders riding over it in purple.
options.viewport: Lunch as terrain; each order a numbered control on a purple course.
options.case: Loses both: the map metaphor needs explaining before the product does.
options.kept: One hue reserved for the single thing that needs action.

options.label: Mixtape J-Card
options.thesis: Lunch as side A and side B, timed so neither side overflows.
options.viewport: The day's slots as a ballpoint tracklist with running totals.
options.case: Loses both: nostalgic rather than local, and handwriting slows reading.
options.kept: Every running total set hard against its limit.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Every order a catalogue number on matte black, names replaced by colour codes.
options.viewport: A pulse plot of demand with order numbers as the only headlines.
options.case: Loses both: coded labels hide exactly what graders need to read.

options.label: Acetate Tab Manual
options.thesis: Each section a coloured divider board with clear acetate leaves above it.
options.viewport: A stepped tab rail down the edge, one tab per stall.
options.case: Loses both: a manual is the wrong object for a lunch app.
options.kept: Each division owns one hue at full strength.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A food-ordering app and a POS dashboard, executed cleanly.
canonCard.viewport: Rounded white cards with dish photos on the phone; KPI tiles and an orders table on the tablet.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from GrabFood or Cates by design.
